title: Block and tackle
prompt: A labelled bench adaptation of the page 57 block and tackle hangs from an external gantry. One continuous rope is fixed at the upper block and reeved alternately through five independently rotating sheaves in the moving lower block and five in the fixed upper block, then over a separate guide wheel to the pulling end. Pull draws ten units of rope for one unit of load rise with an ideal effort of one tenth the moving weight. Add load supports the lower block externally while exchanging the test weight. Lower controls payout by hand. See-through traces all ten supporting rope segments, both axles, the independent sheaves, rope anchor, guide wheel and load hook. Friction and lower-block weight reduce real advantage.
blurb: A bench adaptation of the book’s ten-strand tackle trades a long rope pull for a smaller ideal lifting effort.
truthNotes: One continuous rope, five independent sheaves in each block, a separate guide wheel, and ten supporting legs.
Gantry, support jack, test specimens and disembodied hands are teaching fixtures. Load replacement is a supported specimen operation.
The hand retains the pulling end between strokes and controls payout on Lower.
Small fleet angles are drawn; 10:1 force and travel readouts use the ideal parallel-strand limit. Actual drawn rope length is conserved.
Moving weight includes an illustrative 20 N lower assembly and a 100 N initial test weight. Each spare adds 50 N. Friction is not simulated; real effort is higher.
This is a principle teaching adaptation, not a literal reconstruction or verified edition union.
